### 2026-10-06 – I worked on the starbie project, My laptop is potato so I had to setup kicad on github codespace, which acted up often, I didn't include the time in log where is acted up. I mainly followed the tutori

**2.5h**

I worked on the starbie project, My laptop is potato so I had to setup kicad on github codespace, which acted up often, I didn't include the time in log where is acted up. I mainly followed the tutorial. I know this shouldn't havetaken me this long, but acting up of codespace, then setting the codespace really burned through my time. It wont count towards my logged time but still it is the time I spent. Then in the tutorial, when I started building I noticed some green lines, it took me whole 30 minutes to find that to add those lines I just need to press W, then everything else went smoothly, though I had to retry this project 2 times before the third time I actually was able to build it. This mainly happened because absence of things like SW_PUSH type things in my kicad env, IDK why but it wasn't present, then i fixed the devcontainer because I had ai generated it, thn I again started and it worked. SO yeah... that sums everything up, yes Ik it is more time than you would expect one to take for task like this but you can check the GitHub repo and the dev container files, theirpushes to understadn my struggle

### 2026-10-07 – So today I completed the PCB ROUTING! It took me a longer than expected because the its my first time trying to do the PCB routing. When converting to PCB editor I forgot to add footprints, then that

**1.5h**

So today I completed the PCB ROUTING! It took me a longer than expected because the its my first time trying to do the PCB routing. When converting to PCB editor I forgot to add footprints, then that took a solid 5 minutes, ik very little time but it was the most frustruating time, otherwise everything went smoothly, I didn't run into much errors or anything, it went cools with me. It was kinda fun too. I learned something not mentioned in the tutorial, I can upload images and use it to trace out the shape, I didn't Google that up I promise! I discovered it by accident after I thought that the image button helps me add a prebuilt image, so I foolishly screenshoted the tutorial's image and added it there. I decide to stop and compete the project later as I am currently have caught a cold and fever and its draining the energy out of me. Bye! bye!

### 2026-10-08 – The tutorial had 2 errors in the footprints. Aside from that, in my own work there were around 8 more errors, all being the same that the shape is not closed. That's why that greyish color was not app

**1.5h**

The tutorial had 2 errors in the footprints. Aside from that, in my own work there were around 8 more errors, all being the same that the shape is not closed. That's why that greyish color was not appearing in my PCB layout, I had previously ignored it but then I realized it was actually because of an error, in fact many errors. Soo I started fixing them, first one went fine then second one and all the ones after that were for some reason locked, since I am still  <10 hours experience into kicad I didn't know what locked meant and how to remove it. I entered my issue in claude and it suggested to "Turn on the grid and snap" I pasted this actual thing copy pasted, I still don't know what that exactly means but the I found how to remove it totally by accident. I realized the ones I couldn't edit were purple for some reason. Then I started messing around and I wasn't able to select them, then I randomly saw the selection filter its felt somewhat similar to collision layer of Godot to me sooo I just went ahead and select each one of them thinking now selection should "collide with purple thingy". It worked I was able to select them, then I started messing with them clicking random buttons till I pressed L, I didn't catch it the first time like which specific key caused it but 5-10 minutes later it got clear to me how to lock and unlock things. Yeah!!! I know I am dumb for not knowing unable to finding these basics. But then the story of my stupidity continues, Just to clear one thing I am journaling this long because I ain't got nothing else to do so I am just writing each event that happened in the session so it is going to be a long one. SO Then I fixed the 8 errors I had introduced by my design and it made that faint grey color appear. Then for the sake of God I couldn't find how to fix the 2 errors showed in the tutorial, I just went ahead and messed around a bit longer, thought that it showed footprint, and that too with a specific component so I opened up the footprint editor and somehow even i don't remember but somehow opened the part that was showing error. Then I zoomed in and found it was basically open, since I was samiliar with open and closing of things like these because of the 8 errors I had fixed in the start design, I just went ahead and fixed it quite quickly, though layers was just me color matching the color of the outline of box with the options I got till I found the one which seemed the same. I removed and deleted the old line, thanked my old self for buying 100% keyboard which had the delete and end key, drew a new line and saved. I didn't know how to import this new design into the layout so i just thought it might auto import the updated version like an updated scene in Godot, closed the editor and hoped for best, when I opened the PCB editor and ran DRC it worked, IDK if that's the intended behaviour or not but stilllll, if it was working I was not gonna touch it. SO that was the journey of entire session

### 2026-10-10 – I just completed everything in the STARBIE PROJECT!!!!!! SO this session was all about completing the README and the bom.csv file. Let me give a break down of where my time went in total this session

**1.5h**

I just completed everything in the STARBIE PROJECT!!!!!! SO this session was all about completing the README and the bom.csv file. Let me give a break down of where my time went in total this session took me around 3 hours, but I am going to include the ones where I actually changed a file. So my time was mainly spent in the following things
1. Editing the README
2. Guiding replit on what to make
3. Making prompts
4. clicking images
In this the actual time I included was editing the README, So in the repo there are multiple changes to the README. Replit had created a branch where it kept adding junk content to the README instead of the actual content, like in place of MPU6050 it made the component Gyroscope, there were many other things, I fixed them manually in the replit env. and told it to push the updated content. Then I copied from its branch to the main branch and then  deleted the old branches to clean up the repo.  in the images there is a complete repo
